headline_recommendation.selected_option: TWO-part fix: (A) self-apply operator-preferred design (b) recent-commit pre-push guard to workspace-sync's smart_copy as defense-in-depth (small, well-scoped, harmless even though not the actual culprit). (B) ALSO author integrity-side fix targeting structure-integrity.md Section 7h's open-issues.json self-test — make integrity read+write open-issues.json from its fresh clone exclusively, never from FUSE. HOLD Part B for operator review because the directive scoped the fix to workspace-sync; widening scope to integrity prompt edits warrants explicit operator approval.
headline_recommendation.rationale_one_paragraph: Reconstructing the 01:23–01:30Z incident from the git history shows the open-issues.json revert was committed by integrity (3a709c717, 01:30:38Z), NOT by workspace-sync (42a4628b, 01:27:40Z). Workspace-sync at 01:27:38Z correctly mtime-guard-skipped open-issues.json (its session FUSE had not received decider's ca68cb5d via dome-mirror because dome-mirror runs in a different session's FUSE; ws_mtime < git_time → SKIP). PROP-045's anti-reversion guard is sound and worked as designed. Integrity, however, ran in its own session whose FUSE was also stale, executed Section 7h's self-test which says 'write a corresponding ISS in monitor/decisions/open-issues.json' without specifying clone-vs-FUSE read source, and the Haiku agent's read-modify-write pattern picked up the stale FUSE open-issues.json (pre-ca68cb5), appended ISS-2519, wrote that combined-stale-plus-new content to its clone, and pushed. Integrity completely bypassed workspace-sync's smart_copy, so PROP-045's protection was never invoked. Operator-preferred design (b) — recent-commit pre-push guard — applied universally would have caught this (integrity's push of open-issues.json with a HEAD timestamp <7 min old). Implementing (b) in workspace-sync is defense-in-depth that's pre-approved and small. The actual fix needs to live in structure-integrity.md.
headline_recommendation.scoped_to: Part A (self-applied this run): monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md — add ~25-line recent-commit pre-push guard to smart_copy as defense-in-depth after the existing PROP-045 anti-reversion block. Part B (HELD): monitor/prompts/structure-integrity.md — Section 7h needs an explicit clone-read/clone-write instruction for open-issues.json self-test writes. Operator must approve Part B before tinker self-applies.

executive_summary.problem_one_line: The 2026-06-03T01:30:38Z open-issues.json revert (commit 3a709c71) that erased decider's ca68cb5d EXP-450 closures was caused by INTEGRITY's section 7h self-test bypassing workspace-sync's smart_copy entirely — PROP-045's anti-reversion guard never had a chance to fire because the writer wasn't workspace-sync.
executive_summary.evidence_one_line: Git log shows open-issues.json SHA at ca68cb5d (decider, 01:23:55Z) = a513c66b; SHA at 42a4628b (workspace-sync, 01:27:40Z) = a513c66b (UNCHANGED — workspace-sync didn't touch it); SHA at 3a709c717 (integrity, 01:30:38Z) = e72d31ab (REVERTED — ISS-2273..2279 flipped from assigned-analyst+unblocked_at back to blocked-on-curmudgeon; last_updated reverted from 2026-06-03T01:22:51Z to 2026-06-02T23:11:25Z; ISS-2519 appended). Workspace-sync skip log for 2026-06-03T01:27:38Z contains 43 mtime-guard skips, none for open-issues.json (correctly — FUSE was identical to git at that path, so cmp -s short-circuited before the guard ran). Integrity report at monitor/integrity/report-2026-06-03T02-00.json confirms the integrity run added ISS-2519 to open-issues.json as its Section 7h self-test response.
executive_summary.fix_one_line: Part A — add recent-commit pre-push guard (operator-preferred design (b)) to workspace-sync's smart_copy as defense-in-depth, self-applied this run. Part B — add clone-source-of-truth instruction to structure-integrity.md Section 7h, HELD for operator review because directive scoped the fix to workspace-sync.

Q_H1_race_window.answer: Cron offset mitigation (operator's :30 shift for dome-mirror) reduces probability of the dome-mirror↔workspace-sync race, but the 2026-06-03 incident wasn't caused by that race. workspace-sync correctly handled open-issues.json at 01:27:38Z (the file was unchanged in FUSE vs git — cmp -s short-circuit). The cron offset is still a sound mitigation against a DIFFERENT race (workspace-sync's mtime-guard incorrectly skipping a fresh dome-mirror sync's write), but it doesn't address the actual culprit (integrity).

Q_H2_dome_mirror_didnt_sync_open_issues.answer: Dome-mirror sentinel at 01:26:59Z DID copy 88 files (sync_exit_code=0) into its OWN session FUSE (/sessions/modest-vibrant-brahmagupta/mnt/dome-model-review). Cross-session FUSE staleness applies: dome-mirror updated its session FUSE, but workspace-sync ran in a different session whose FUSE was independently stale. This is the standard cross-session pattern documented in CLAUDE.md ('Each scheduled task runs in its own per-session /sessions/<id>/mnt/dome-model-review/ FUSE mount.'). Same cross-session pattern affected integrity at 01:30:38Z.

Q_H3_PROP_045_guard_bypassed.answer: PROP-045's guard didn't bypass — it correctly skipped open-issues.json at workspace-sync's 01:27:38Z run via the cmp -s short-circuit (FUSE identical to git, so guard didn't need to fire). The bypass is structural: the actual revert was committed by INTEGRITY at 01:30:38Z, and integrity does not call smart_copy. PROP-045 protects ONE writer (workspace-sync); the other writers (integrity, decider, analyst) push directly from their own clones and the guard isn't in their code path.

Q_H4_workspace_sync_FUSE_pre_dome_mirror.answer: Plausible but moot for this incident. workspace-sync at 01:27 successfully avoided pushing stale open-issues.json (its FUSE was either identical to git or correctly mtime-guarded). The bug is downstream at integrity.

Q_H5_actual_cause_new_hypothesis.answer: H5 (CORRECT): the FUSE-revert was committed by INTEGRITY (3a709c71), not workspace-sync (42a4628b). Integrity's Section 7h self-test ('if the scan flags ≥1 entry, write a corresponding ISS in monitor/decisions/open-issues.json') doesn't specify whether the read source is FUSE or clone. Haiku-model integrity reads from FUSE (cwd-relative default), modifies in-memory to append ISS-2519, writes the modified blob to its clone (replacing the clone's fresh ca68cb5d-based copy), and pushes. The decider's own 03:20:11Z self-heal note in commit 3d6d2d19 ALSO misattributed the bug to workspace-sync ('workspace-sync had overwritten ca68cb5's open-issues with stale FUSE copy'). The misattribution propagated to the operator's directive. Tinker is the first agent to surface H5.

Q_self_apply_or_hold.answer: PARTIAL SELF-APPLY. Part A (workspace-sync recent-commit guard) is operator-pre-approved (design (b)), well-scoped, ~25 LOC, harmless defense-in-depth even though not the actual culprit — self-apply this run. Part B (integrity prompt fix) targets structure-integrity.md which is OUTSIDE the directive's stated scope (the directive specifically says 'The fix is in workspace-sync's anti-reversion logic, not dome-mirror's prompt' — Part B is on a third prompt the directive didn't mention). Per directive Step 7 hold-condition: 'if tinker discovers the underlying race needs architectural redesign rather than guard-tweak.' This finding (wrong agent identified) qualifies. HOLD Part B.

phase_1_design.scope_part_A: Single-file edit: monitor/prompts/workspace-sync.md, smart_copy helper. Add a recent-commit pre-push guard after the existing PROP-045 anti-reversion block. The guard: before copying FUSE→clone, look at `git log -1 --format=%ct -- $dst` (HEAD commit timestamp on this path). If that timestamp is within the last RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW_SEC (300s = 5 min), SKIP the copy with reason 'recent-commit-guard; git HEAD on path is <5min old'. The skipped FUSE write is recoverable in the next ws-sync cycle (1 hour later) when the window has elapsed. Genuine pre-existing FUSE→git rescue is not blocked because the decider's commit-and-push-then-rescue-via-FUSE pattern only triggers when git push 403s (push fails); the FUSE write is the recovery, not the source.
phase_1_design.scope_part_B_NOT_APPLIED: Two-file edit: monitor/prompts/structure-integrity.md + (optionally) the Section 7h self-test. Add a PROLOGUE block: 'When writing to monitor/decisions/open-issues.json (Sections 7a.5 and 7h self-tests), ALWAYS read AND write via your fresh clone at ${CLONE_DIR}/monitor/decisions/open-issues.json, NEVER via FUSE. FUSE may be stale due to cross-session staleness during cron overlap with decider/dome-mirror. The clone is authoritative.' Plus a worked example showing the clone-relative path pattern.

report_field_addition_part_A: Tinker's soft-complaints grep should flag any run where recent_commit_guard > 0 — that is a signal that another writer just committed within 5 min. Sustained recent_commit_guard > 5 per cycle indicates over-aggressive other writers and warrants a writer-side rate-limit (separate PROP).
operational_notes_part_A: - Recent-commit pre-push guard (PROP-077): the smart_copy helper checks `git log -1 --format=%ct -- $dst` before pushing FUSE→git. If origin's HEAD commit on this path is <5 min old, the push is skipped with 'recent-commit-guard'. This protects against the cross-writer race where another agent commits and workspace-sync's session FUSE hasn't yet propagated the commit. Note: this is DEFENSE IN DEPTH for the 2026-06-03T01:30Z incident — the actual revert came from integrity, not workspace-sync. See PROP-077 for the H5 root-cause analysis and the integrity-side proposed fix (Part B, held for operator review).

regression_check_part_A.before: smart_copy with mtime guard + PROP-045 anti-reversion. The 2026-06-03 incident is NOT a workspace-sync bug — workspace-sync correctly avoided pushing open-issues.json at 01:27 — so Part A wouldn't have prevented this incident even if deployed earlier.
regression_check_part_A.after: smart_copy with mtime guard + PROP-045 anti-reversion + PROP-077 recent-commit guard. Protects against a FUTURE failure mode where (a) decider commits, (b) workspace-sync's FUSE shows newer mtime than git_time but content matches no historic commit (passes anti-reversion), (c) workspace-sync would push the stale content. The recent-commit guard adds a temporal safety property: 'if the file just changed in git, wait one cycle before considering FUSE writes.'
preserved_behaviors: Universal-pusher rescue path for decider 403 push failures — TRADE-OFF: the rescue is delayed by up to 5 min on files where the decider just attempted a push. But decider's push-failure block writes to FUSE only AFTER the push 403's; ws_mtime is updated by that write, and origin HEAD timestamp on the file is from the LAST SUCCESSFUL push (>5 min ago in most cases). So the rescue is preserved in practice.
JSON-validity gate (PROP-024) — runs in pre-push integrity gate, unaffected.
Mtime guard — runs FIRST; recent-commit-guard is an additional check after anti-reversion.
Anti-reversion (PROP-045) — runs BEFORE recent-commit-guard; both fire independently.
regression_check_part_A.edge_case_decider_403_rescue: If decider's push 403s and decider writes the committed-but-unpushed file to FUSE, ws_mtime updates immediately. origin/main HEAD timestamp on the file is the LAST SUCCESSFUL push time, which is from BEFORE this run. So head_ts is OLD (>5min), the recent-commit guard does NOT fire, and the rescue path proceeds. Verified by reasoning, not by test.

directive_specified_scope_to_workspace_s.objection: The directive explicitly scopes the fix to workspace-sync.md and lists three pre-approved fix directions (a)/(b)/(c) all targeting workspace-sync. Should tinker just apply (b) and call it done?
directive_specified_scope_to_workspace_s.response: Step 5 of the directive explicitly invites the possibility of a 5th hypothesis: 'Tinker may discover the actual cause is a 5th hypothesis. Document it.' Step 7 explicitly invites HOLD: 'Hold for operator review if a Q-OP needs answering or if tinker discovers the underlying race needs architectural redesign rather than guard-tweak.' Applying (b) to workspace-sync without surfacing H5 would leave the integrity bug in place; the next time integrity runs while open-issues.json was recently committed by decider, the revert recurs. The directive's safety-first framing supports HOLD on Part B until operator confirms scope expansion.

why_self_apply_part_A_if_not_the_culprit.objection: If integrity is the actual culprit, why bother editing workspace-sync at all?
why_self_apply_part_A_if_not_the_culprit.response: Defense in depth has independent value. Workspace-sync IS exposed to the same race class (a writer pushes; workspace-sync's session FUSE is briefly stale; workspace-sync attempts to push) — the 2026-06-03 incident just wasn't an instance of it. The operator-pre-approved (b) design is well-targeted to that class. Code is small (~25 LOC) and additive. Even if Part B is the actual fix, Part A makes workspace-sync more robust against future variants. Operator's pre-approval makes self-apply safe.

part_B_could_be_in_a_followup_PROP.objection: Part B targets a different prompt — would it be cleaner as a separate PROP?
part_B_could_be_in_a_followup_PROP.response: Yes, and that's the operator's call. Part B is documented in detail here so the operator has the full diagnosis in one place. If the operator approves the integrity-side fix, it can be implemented as either an amendment to this PROP or a fresh PROP. Tinker recommends a fresh PROP with status='operator-approved' and a follow-up directive that explicitly authorizes structure-integrity.md edits.

could_decider_self_heal_be_made_more_pro.objection: Decider's 03:20 self-heal worked. Why not just make it run faster?
could_decider_self_heal_be_made_more_pro.response: Decider's self-heal is a 1-2 hour reactive band-aid that depends on the duplicate-detect heuristic still being correct. The actual fix (Part B) prevents the revert in the first place, eliminating the need for self-heal on this class. Self-heal remains as a backstop. Speeding up decider's heal would help, but only marginally — the right fix is upstream at the writer.

what_about_cross_session_FUSE_in_general.objection: Cross-session FUSE staleness is a systemic issue. Is there an architectural fix?
what_about_cross_session_FUSE_in_general.response: Yes, and it's already deployed: PROP-061 (Step 4c git→FUSE propagation, succeeded by PROP-066's helper-script extraction). But Step 4c runs HOURLY (one workspace-sync cycle) and the 2026-06-03 incident happened in a 5-minute window between decider's push and integrity's run. The systemic fix would be a per-second/per-minute FUSE-refresh poller, which is more infrastructure than the operator wants. The pragmatic fix is to make each writer read from its own clone (which is always fresh-pulled at run start).

related_mitigations.cron_offset_dome_mirror: Operator updated dome-mirror cron from '0 * * * *' to '30 * * * *' on 2026-06-03 ~04:55Z (via mcp__scheduled-tasks__update_scheduled_task, reflected in task description). Per directive Step 11: 'document the cron-offset change... in the PROP file's related mitigations section as a near-term operator-side action.' The offset reduces the dome-mirror↔workspace-sync race window from ~40s to ~27 min, but it does NOT address integrity (which fires at 02:00Z, well after both). Offset can be reverted to :00 after Part B lands and the integrity-side bug is eliminated, per directive non-goal #5 (do not revert until proven across 2-3 days).

phase_1_enforce_directly.behavior: Recent-commit guard fires, LOGS to skip-log with reason 'recent-commit-guard', SKIPS the copy. Guard is conservative (300s window); false positives are limited to cases where another writer just committed within 5 min, which is what we want to skip.
phase_1_enforce_directly.rationale: Operator pre-approved design (b). Small additive change with sound failure mode (skip is the safe default — file gets pushed on the next cycle when the window elapses). Shadow mode unnecessary because the check is a temporal property of git state, not a content-equivalence check that could false-positive on legitimate idempotent writes.

Q_OP_for_operator: Q_OP_1: APPROVE Part B (integrity prompt edits)? Affirmative → tinker drafts follow-up PROP and self-applies on next run. Negative → tinker accepts residual integrity-side risk; recurrence is caught only by decider's self-heal.
Q_OP_2: Once Part B lands and proves stable for 2-3 days, REVERT dome-mirror cron from :30 back to :00? Per directive non-goal #5, no automatic revert; explicit operator decision required.

Q_OP_3: Should the recent-commit guard window (RECENT_COMMIT_WINDOW_SEC=300) be tuned? Tinker chose 300s as conservative-safe; lower values (60s) reduce false-skip rate but tighter race window; higher values (600s) widen safety margin but delay legitimate FUSE-side rescue. Tinker recommends 300s; operator may override.

Q_OP_4: Should similar pre-push guards be added to decider, analyst, integrity, and other writers' prompts for symmetric protection? Risk: prompt-bloat across many agents to fix what is, fundamentally, a clone-vs-FUSE-read-source question per writer. Tinker recommends: just fix integrity (Part B) for now; revisit other writers if recurrence shows up at a different agent.
notes_for_operator: DIRECTIVE-20260603-002 assumed workspace-sync was the culprit based on the decider's 03:20 self-heal note (which itself misattributed). The git evidence is unambiguous: 42a4628b (workspace-sync, 01:27) did NOT modify open-issues.json. 3a709c71 (integrity, 01:30) DID. PROP-045 worked correctly.

The H5 finding is a propagation-of-error story: integrity wrote stale content; decider's self-heal interpreted the resulting state as a workspace-sync overwrite (plausible reading without git-log forensics); operator drafted a workspace-sync-scoped directive based on the self-heal note. Tinker is the first agent with both forensic access and the time to verify.
Part A is harmless even though it's not the actual fix — operator-pre-approved, small, well-targeted to a real race class.
Part B is the actual fix. Operator review is warranted because it expands the directive's scope (structure-integrity.md was not in the original scope).

If Part B is approved, tinker recommends accompanying it with a one-line PROLOGUE to the integrity prompt that escalates the clone-vs-FUSE distinction. Haiku agents need explicit guidance; the existing prompt leaves the choice ambiguous.
